text:
maria: quick sync — I've been seeing persistent tiny free fragments after high-concurrency decode bursts, causing >15% stuck GPU residency despite overall free memory being ~30%
jon: ugh, same. appears when mixed short+long seq batches interleave. small slabs (<=4KB) never coalesce fast enough
sasha: thought we had aggressive coalescing? maybe the background merge is low priority under load
chen: right — current policy: merge_interval=60s and cpu-priority=low. under burst it gets starved. propose adaptive merge on memory pressure + sample-based scoring
maria: sketch: when eviction backlog > X or gpu-residency > Y%, switch merge to immediate for hot slab classes, and optionally compact adjacent free runs
jon: sample scoring sounds good. we can track fragmentation score per arena: frag = 1 - largest_free_block / total_free_in_arena. threshold >0.7 => trigger
sasha: also consider split-on-alloc for big requests to avoid leaving small unusable tail pieces. tradeoff is extra bookkeeping/time
chen: config prototype (pseudo):
```
allocator.compaction: {
  pressure_threshold: 0.6,
  fast_merge_classes: [32,64,128,256],
  scan_window_ms: 200,
  max_background_threads: 4
}
```
maria: would like to wire this into residency controller so we don't fight eviction heuristics. if merge frees up contiguous blocks we can favor host->gpu page migration for pinned workloads
jon: one more worry — repeated merge/split churn could thrash CPU cycles on tiny allocs. need conservative backoff and metrics: merge_ops/sec, bytes_reclaimed, cpu_millis
sasha: +1 on metrics. add a per-class cooldown and only escalate if bytes_reclaimed_per_sec > epsilon for 3 samples
allocator-bot: scheduled job created: "frag-merge-experiment" starts in canary on dedicated pool tomorrow 03:00 UTC :rocket:
chen: sweet. I'll add logging flags and a perf microbenchmark that simulates mixed decode+streaming loads
maria: ok let's run canary, gather merge_ops, reclaimed bytes, post metrics here. if good we'll cut an RFC for API and defaults. thanks folks :thumbsup:
